items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new helper `punycode(domain)` has a clear name and a docstring. Call sites keep their `# IDN -> ACE` comments, and the formatting matches the existing code. The patch is effectively the same as the reference.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One helper in django/utils/encoding.py replaces the copy-pasted `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` calls in mail, validators and html. There is no dead code. The one extra change, adding the reporter's name to AUTHORS, is harmless.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The existing `except UnicodeError` handlers in validators and html are kept. `punycode(socket.getfqdn())` has no try/except, so a malformed hostname raises an error instead of being hidden. This matches the reference behavior.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: The conversion happens once, at the source: `self._fqdn = punycode(socket.getfqdn())` in CachedDnsName, so it works for every encoding. The agent checked that ASCII names stay the same (`punycode("example.com") == "example.com"`). Nothing suppresses errors.
